markers.title: Named stages, in the order the work happens
markers.finding: The old form asked for the outcome before the event, and classification errors were flagged back from above after the fact.
markers.decision: The record runs on five named stages and shows which one is current. Classification stays locked until the welfare check is recorded, so severity is set from what happened rather than from a guess.
markers.rejected: A free status dropdown the manager can set to anything at any time, which is how misclassification happened.

markers.title: Speak to the person first
markers.finding: Team members told their manager first and trusted them. The barrier to reporting was the form, the phone and the threshold, not fear of the manager.
markers.decision: The first thing the record asks of the manager is a welfare check, with a deadline tied to the end of the reporter's shift rather than to a business day.
markers.rejected: Opening the record on the classification form, which treats the report as paperwork before it is treated as a person who got hurt.

markers.title: What happened, and how
markers.finding: Incident type came first on the old form, with options such as first aid or lost time that nobody can predict while their hand is under the cold tap.
markers.decision: The record opens with the mechanism in the reporter's own terms: what happened, how, body part, equipment, when and where. Every field is something the person could answer at the time.
markers.rejected: Keeping the industrial taxonomy and adding help text and examples to each field. The categories were the problem, not the labelling.

markers.title: What the report cost the reporter
markers.finding: Managers said a report takes one to three minutes. The cost people actually felt was stepping off the floor during a rush and needing permission to do it.
markers.decision: The record states how long the report took and that nothing was asked which the reporter could not answer, so the cost of reporting is measured on every report rather than argued about.
markers.rejected: Duration metrics as a separate analytics panel, which nobody in a restaurant opens.

markers.title: Severity is a judgement about the outcome
markers.finding: The notifiable-to-the-regulator question sent people to a compliance matrix, and even area safety leads admitted asking the restaurant's safety champion which option to choose.
markers.decision: Classification sits after the welfare check, is set by the manager from the outcome, and states plainly that the reporter was never asked. The regulator question appears only when the outcome makes it relevant, with the matrix answered from the record.
markers.rejected: Asking the regulator question on the reporter's form, where it produced errors that came back as criticism.

markers.title: The report cannot close without naming the fix
markers.finding: Minor reports were closed without a word, which built the belief that reporting helps you with a claim but does nothing for anyone else.
markers.decision: Corrective actions are part of the record, each with an owner, a due date and evidence required on close, so closing a report means saying what was done about it.
markers.rejected: A separate actions module with no link back to the report that caused it.
markers.pattern: Jira, work item with linked items — https://mobbin.com/screens/e06dbe4d-6a5d-4808-94f1-8ce7fa26f9d1

markers.title: The message back is drafted, not automatic
markers.finding: Reporters rarely heard what changed. The safety team's view on incentives was blunt: put an incentive on hazard reports and you get reports, not hazards. Recognising outcomes was the proposal that survived.
markers.decision: The message to the reporter is drafted from the corrective actions and shown on the record before it is sent, so the manager can see and edit the sentence that names the fix.
markers.rejected: An automatic 'your report was closed' notification, which is the silence people already described, with a timestamp on it.
markers.pattern: Pipedrive, record history with activity entries — https://mobbin.com/screens/6178b5a8-b478-4aed-99bc-d74b07a68383

markers.title: The pattern at this station, while it still matters
markers.finding: Reporting volume varied a lot between restaurants. Low volume could mean a safe restaurant or a silent one, and the platform's data could not tell the difference.
markers.decision: The record shows the reports already made at the same station over eight weeks, so a second burn at fryer 2 is visible while the manager is deciding what to do about this one.
markers.rejected: Site-level totals only, which is the number that could not tell a safe restaurant from a silent one.
markers.pattern: Airtable, projects dashboard with inline bars — https://mobbin.com/screens/53a16902-f7a3-47f5-859e-20cd4891e72d
